section: A conditional corridor and decisive research gates
paragraphs: The proposed corridor is a research target, not a transport device. Its prescribed geometry separates preparation from carriage, so a source could be predeployed or arrive from outside. Neither option has been shown to work. The decisive question is whether the geometric shortcut can survive source dynamics, propagation, quantum effects, and operational control in one consistent model.

Gate 1: source dynamics. A candidate must reproduce the required density, momentum flux, and spatial stresses from a specified action and complete admissible initial data, while satisfying the coupled gravity–matter equations. Defining stress from the Einstein tensor does not construct such a source. The canonical scalar and the regular, minimally coupled single-scalar $P(X,\phi)$ class examined here fail under the stated positive-energy and common-Cauchy-slicing assumptions. A new candidate must change the action, target geometry, or those assumptions and justify the replacement; changing preparation alone does not remove a local source incompatibility. Complete vacuum data also cannot yield the prescribed pulse in an autonomous theory with unique Cauchy development.

Gate 2: finite-duration propagation. The eternal constant-speed geometry exhibits a restricted axial-ray obstruction, but that result cannot simply be transferred to a switched pulse. The proposed test is to calculate affine-frequency evolution and parallelly propagated curvature through a finite episode, including whether the relevant spatial velocity gradient has a sufficiently bounded time integral. That criterion remains unproved. Even a frequency bound would leave affine completeness, nonaxial rays, complete-ray energy integrals, and tidal exposure to be checked separately. A negative integral on an incomplete ray is not a global averaged-null-energy theorem.

Gate 3: quantum backreaction. For a specified field theory and state, one must fix boundary and renormalization conditions, calculate stress and fluctuations on the finite-duration configuration, and then show either a self-consistent coupled solution or a controlled backreaction bound. The classical negative-stress and blueshift calculations do not establish a universal quantum prohibition or quantum safety. A fixed-background calculation is therefore an intermediate screen, not the end of this gate.

Gate 4: preparation and control. A proposed system must show which source regions can receive control signals during formation, transit, switching, and shutdown, especially at the leading wall. Predeployment changes the architecture but still needs admissible data and an executable control law. Perturbative and nonlinear stability of the coupled system must also be assessed. The temporal function proved for one prescribed corridor does not settle the causality of multiple corridors or repeated trips.

Gate 5: empirical comparison. Only a sufficiently specified interacting theory can be tested against observations and the domain literature. No such dataset or original literature assessment is supplied here. The wider-cone alternative additionally needs interacting source, detector, and gravitational sectors before its feasibility can be compared at the same depth. The next discriminating tasks are to identify a source that escapes the stated exclusions without sacrificing well-posed evolution, and to test whether finite switching removes the eternal propagation obstruction. Passing either task alone would not establish a workable drive; failing one would reject that particular source–target combination, not every possible shortcut framework.
